name: Wandalbertus Prumiensis
untranslatedHighlights: Martyrology in verse (c. 848), Life of St. Goar, supplementary poems on months, agricultural labor, seasons, church Hours

name: Anselmus Lucensis
untranslatedHighlights: Collectio canonum (1081-1083), Liber contra Wibertum; important Gregorian Reform canonical works

name: Ludovicus I Franciae
modernTranslations: Thegan's Deeds of Emperor Louis, Life of Louis by 'the Astronomer', Ermoldus Nigellus's Poem in Honor of Louis—all translated by Thomas F. X. Noble (Penn State University Press)
untranslatedHighlights: These are biographies ABOUT Louis, not his own compositions; his own letter collections and edicts not located in English translation

name: Philastrius Brixiensis
untranslatedHighlights: Diversarum hereseon liber (c. 384)—catalogue of 128 Christian and 28 Jewish heresies; Polish translation exists but no English

name: Placidus Nonantulani
untranslatedHighlights: Glossary (medieval Latin lexical work); textual history studied but no English translation found

name: Gaufridus Grossus
modernTranslations: The Life of Blessed Bernard of Tiron (Vita Bernardi Tironiensis, c. 1147), first English translation by Ruth Harwood Cline, Catholic University of America Press (2009)

name: Egbertus Eboracensis
untranslatedHighlights: Works attributed in Middle Ages (Paenitentiale Ecgberhti, pontifical, canons) not authenticated by modern scholars; no English translation

name: Cardinalis de Aragonia
untranslatedHighlights: Nicolai Cardinalis de Aragonia; collections of papal history excerpts; identity and authorship partially uncertain

name: Thiofridus Efternacensis
untranslatedHighlights: Flores epytaphii sanctorum (c. 1104/5) on relics; hagiographical works; no English translation located

name: Gerardus Itherius
untranslatedHighlights: Gérard Ithier, 7th prior of Grandmont (1188-1198); Speculum Grandimontis compilation (Vita of Stephen of Muret, his thoughts/maxims, canonization account) and De institutione novitiorum adaptation; no English translation located

name: Auctor incertus (Cassiodorus Vivariensis?)
untranslatedHighlights: Attribution uncertain; if Cassiodorus, some works translated; unclear which PL entry applies

name: Eligius Noviomensis
pdTranslations: Partial English translation of Vita S. Eligius by Jo Ann McNamara (translation of Dado's biography, not Eligius's own works)
modernTranslations: Extended incomplete version online at Fordham Medieval Sourcebook; McNamara partial translation in Head (ed.) Medieval Hagiography (2001)
untranslatedHighlights: Eligius's own letters and sermons not located in English translation; most sources discuss his life (Vita by Dado)

name: Braulio Caesaraugustanus
untranslatedHighlights: Completed works of Isidore (Etymologies in 20 books), Life of St. Emilian, hymns, letter collection; no English translation found

name: Folcardus Sithivensis
untranslatedHighlights: Hagiographer (fl. 1080); Miracula Sancti Bertini; works preserved in Latin only

name: Usuardus Sangermanensis
untranslatedHighlights: Martyrologium (c. 875); 1100+ saints' lives; became basis for Roman Martyrology; no complete English translation located

name: Ademarus Cibardi
modernTranslations: Limited online: 'Adhemar of Chabannes' Commemoratio abbatum Lemovicensium' translation mentioned on blog; full extent unclear
untranslatedHighlights: Chronicon Aquitanicum et Francicum, Commemoratio (c. 1026) on Abbey of Saint-Martial; most works remain in Latin

name: Valerianus Cemeliensis
untranslatedHighlights: De bono disciplinae (disputed authorship); medieval attribution to Augustine-circle figures; no English translation

name: Novatianus
pdTranslations: Treatise on the Trinity (De trinitate) in CCEL Ante-Nicene Fathers series (ANF05); 19th-century translation, public domain

name: Widukindus Corbeiensis
modernTranslations: Deeds of the Saxons (Res gestae Saxonicae), translated by Bernard S. Bachrach and David S. Bachrach, Medieval Texts in Translation series

name: Carolus II Calvus
untranslatedHighlights: 9th-century Carolingian emperor; various documents/letters in PL; no dedicated English translation collection located

name: Jonas Bobiensis
modernTranslations: Jonas of Bobbio: Life of Columbanus, Life of John of Réomé, and Life of Vedast, translated by Alexander O'Hara and Ian Wood, Translated Texts for Historians vol. 64 (Liverpool University Press)

name: Wicbodus
untranslatedHighlights: Wigbod (8th c.): Quaestiones in Octateuchum, encyclopedic Genesis/Octateuch commentary composed for Charlemagne at Lorsch (775-800), compiled from eight Church Fathers, with prefatory hexameter poems; no English translation located

name: Lupus de Olmeto
untranslatedHighlights: Regula monachorum ex scriptis Hieronymi collecta (15th c.); manuscripts at Bodleian and BnF; no English translation

name: Joannes Venetus
modernTranslations: Italian translation of Istoria Veneticorum exists (1999) but no English version located
untranslatedHighlights: Istoria Veneticorum (c. 1008), first history of Venice; no English, French, or international translation published

name: Gregorius Nyssenus
pdTranslations: Some older Latin translations (15th c., e.g., George of Trebizond's De vita Moysis, 1446)
modernTranslations: Life of Moses (De vita Moysis), translated with notes by Abraham J. Malherbe and Everett Ferguson, Paulist Press (1978); various individual works in CCEL and other collections

name: Bonizo Placentinus
modernTranslations: Annotated translation of Liber ad amicum ('Book...To a Friend') in The Papal Reform of the Eleventh Century (Manchester University Press); requires institutional access
untranslatedHighlights: Other works not fully translated; Liber ad amicum is primary work but translation appears limited/academic

name: Concilia Romana
pdTranslations: Early council texts translated in NPNF series (e.g., Nicene Council); various collections
modernTranslations: The Seven Ecumenical Councils of the Undivided Church (325–787) available in English; Conciliorum Oecumenicorum Decreta (Greek/Latin with English apparatus)
untranslatedHighlights: Anonymous/collective category; specific Roman councils vary in translation coverage

name: Chrodegangus Metensis
pdTranslations: Old English version of the enlarged Rule of Chrodegang (early medieval, pre-Conquest); Internet Archive edition
modernTranslations: The Chrodegang Rules: The Rules for the Common Life of the Secular Clergy from the Eighth and Ninth Centuries, translated with critical texts and commentary by Jerome Bertram (Routledge)

name: Auctor incertus (Anselmus Cantuariensis?)
pdTranslations: Pseudo-Anselmian meditations/prayers circulated with authentic ones and were included in the 19th-c. English translation 'St. Anselm's Book of Meditations and Prayers' (trans. M.R.)
modernTranslations: Benedicta Ward's Penguin Classics 'Prayers and Meditations of St Anselm' translates only the authentic core, excluding most pseudo-Anselm material
untranslatedHighlights: Attribution uncertain; pseudo-Anselmian devotional corpus studied (e.g., by Sarah McNamer) but much untranslated as a distinct body

name: Auctor incertus (Leo I?)
pdTranslations: Authentic Leo I sermons/letters translated in NPNF (public domain); pseudo-Leo material generally excluded from those translations
modernTranslations: FOTC vol. 93 (Leo the Great: Sermons) covers authentic sermons; large pseudo-epigraphic sermon corpus attributed to Leo remains untranslated
untranslatedHighlights: Attribution uncertain; sermons circulated in medieval homiliaries under Leo's name with uncertain origin (per roger-pearse.com bibliographical note)

name: Leo III
modernTranslations: The Letters of Pope Leo III (English translations of all ten letters, with Latin originals; Amazon/self-published)
untranslatedHighlights: Some works (diplomatic/state correspondence) translated; broader theological works may remain in Latin

name: Odilo Suessionensis
modernTranslations: Extract (chs. 44-45) of the Translatio sancti Sebastiani (c. 930) translated in English for a UBC history teaching resource
untranslatedHighlights: Liber de translatione reliquiarum S. Sebastiani martyris et Gregorii I papae (BHL 7545); bulk of work untranslated

name: Alanus Antissiodorensis
untranslatedHighlights: Bishop of Auxerre (1152–1167); Life of St. Bernard attributed to him; no English translation located

name: Goscelinus Cantuariensis
untranslatedHighlights: Hagiographer (c. 1035–1107); Liber confortatorius and saints' lives; no dedicated modern English translation located

name: Luculentus

name: Guigo V prior Carthusiae
modernTranslations: Scala Claustralium ('Ladder of Four Rungs') / The Ladder of Divine Ascent, translated into Middle English and modern English; Paulist Press edition

name: Adrianus II
untranslatedHighlights: Pope Adrian II (792–872); diplomatic and papal correspondence; no dedicated English translation of his works

name: Petrus Tudebodus
modernTranslations: Historia de Hierosolymitano itinere translated by John Hugh Hill and Laurita L. Hill (1974), Memoirs of the American Philosophical Society

name: Aimoinus Sangermanensis
